claim: [L1] (LOW/nonportable type declaration) The lookup table is declared with the nonstandard `real*8` form rather than an explicit project or `iso_fortran_env` kind, making its precision compiler-dependent.
other_wording: [L1-L6602] (MED/kind-portability) The declaration uses the nonstandard REAL*8 form while every constructor literal lacks an explicit double-precision kind, so the constructor is formed from default-real constants before conversion to the declared element kind.

claim: [L1] (LOW/nonportable type declaration) The lookup table is declared with the nonstandard `real*8` form rather than an explicit project or `iso_fortran_env` kind, making its precision compiler-dependent.
other_wording: [L1-L3962] (MED/kind-portability) The parameter uses nonstandard REAL*8 while all constructor constants are unkinded default-real literals, so their values are rounded at default-real precision before conversion to the declared element kind.

claim: [L2-L3,L56-L58,L84-L91,L94-L98] (MED/unchecked MPI failures) MPI return codes are overwritten without inspection, allowing communicator, datatype, collective, or free errors to cascade through invalid handles and incomplete data.
other_wording: [L2-L3,L56-L58,L84-L86,L90-L91,L95,L98] (MED/unchecked-mpi-status) Every MPI call overwrites ier without checking it, so communicator, datatype-construction, collective, or cleanup failures can be silently followed by further MPI operations.

claim: [L5-L8] (LOW/overbroad abort scope) A bad root for the supplied communicator aborts `MPI_COMM_WORLD` rather than `comm`, terminating ranks outside a subcommunicator invocation.
other_wording: [L5-L8] (MED/communicator-mismatch) A root error detected for the supplied comm communicator aborts MPI_COMM_WORLD instead of comm, unexpectedly terminating ranks outside a subcommunicator.

claim: [L6-L9] (LOW/overbroad abort scope) A bad root for the supplied communicator aborts `MPI_COMM_WORLD` rather than `comm`, unexpectedly terminating ranks outside a subcommunicator that invoked this routine.
other_wording: [L6-L9] (MED/communicator-mismatch) Invalid root handling aborts MPI_COMM_WORLD rather than the supplied comm communicator, which can terminate unrelated ranks when comm is a subcommunicator.

claim: [L2-L3,L44-L46,L59-L66,L69-L73] (MED/unchecked MPI failures) All MPI error codes are overwritten without inspection, so communicator, datatype-construction, commit, collective, or free failures can cascade into use or freeing of invalid datatype handles.
other_wording: [L2-L3,L44-L46,L59-L61,L65-L66,L70,L73] (MED/unchecked-mpi-status) MPI return codes are repeatedly overwritten and never tested, allowing communicator, datatype, collective, or cleanup failures to remain undetected.

claim: [L2-L9,L34-L36] (LOW/invalid address for empty array) For every array the template unconditionally takes `c_loc` of its lower-bound element, which does not exist when any generated variable has zero total size.
other_wording: [L2-L9,L36] (MED/zero-size-array-address) For every array the template takes C_LOC of the element at its lower bounds without checking SIZE, which is an invalid element reference when any generated array is empty.

claim: [L17,L27-L38] (MED/stale output on lookup failure) The output pointer is `intent(inout)` and is never initialized to `C_NULL_PTR`, so an unknown name or any mismatch between `chartoindex` and the generated cases returns the caller's previous or uninitialized pointer value.
other_wording: [L27-L28,L31-L38] (MED/stale-output-on-failure) Unknown names and recognized names absent from the generated select cases return without assigning x, so the caller can retain an unrelated incoming pointer with no status result.

claim: [L5,L10] (LOW/hard-coded dimension contract) The output extent is declared with `MAXDIMS` but initialized with a fixed six-element constructor, so the template silently assumes `MAXDIMS == 6` and becomes nonconforming if that parameter changes.
other_wording: [L5,L10] (HIGH/shape-conformance) The dummy array extent is MAXDIMS but it is assigned a fixed six-element constructor, which is nonconforming unless MAXDIMS is exactly 6.

claim: [L18,L50-L54] (MED/unchecked foreign pointer) The public C binding passes `xptr` directly to `c_f_pointer` and then dereferences the resulting Fortran pointer without checking for `C_NULL_PTR`, so a null caller pointer causes invalid pointer use instead of a controlled failure.
other_wording: [L18,L49-L54] (HIGH/unchecked-c-pointer) xptr is converted and dereferenced without first checking C_ASSOCIATED, so a null C pointer can be used as the source of an array or scalar assignment.

claim: [L75,L79-L82] (MED/unchecked internal I/O failure) Every generated logger writes arbitrary caller content and format text into a fixed-length `display` buffer without `IOSTAT`, so an overlong record or invalid format can turn logging itself into a fatal runtime I/O error.
other_wording: [L75,L79-L83] (MED/unchecked-internal-io) Both list-directed and caller-formatted writes target a fixed-length display buffer without IOSTAT/IOMSG handling, so an invalid format or output longer than slen can raise a runtime I/O failure during logging.
